memory_update.text: CoreWeave should remain the reference benchmark for specialized AI cloud capacity, but not dominate underfollowed discovery because it is now high-attention and large-cap.
Applied Digital is a second-order capacity candidate where the primary chokepoint is power-ready AI/HPC colocation leased to neocloud customers, especially CoreWeave.
IREN is a shadow-capacity candidate because legacy bitcoin-mining infrastructure, secured power, and self-owned data centers may be repurposed into AI cloud GPU services.
Nebius is a direct neocloud candidate with dedicated GPU cluster contracts; further work should stress-test customer concentration, capex funding, and utilization.
Layer 2 should verify which candidates have binding customer contracts versus illustrative ARR targets, and should separate contracted megawatts from speculative power pipeline.

node: Specialized AI cloud and scarce compute capacity providers
summary: Expanded the universe around scarce ready-to-use AI compute capacity rather than GPU ownership alone. The two-lane list uses CoreWeave as the obvious reference anchor, then maps less obvious US-listed public exposures where the chokepoint may be secured power, liquid-cooled data-center buildout, contracted AI/HPC leasing, or vertically integrated GPU cloud operations. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
